topic: Latency optimisation via connection reuse and warm capacity
question_text: A Lambda-based Bedrock service suffers intermittent high latency: some invocations pay a cold-start penalty, and per-request TLS handshakes to Bedrock add overhead under load. Which two techniques most directly reduce these latency sources?

options.text: Enable Lambda provisioned concurrency to eliminate cold starts on the critical path
Reuse a pooled Bedrock client/HTTP connection across invocations instead of creating one per request
Add more denied topics to the guardrail

explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps Lambda execution environments warm, removing cold-start latency for latency-sensitive endpoints, and reusing a pooled client/connection (initialised outside the handler) avoids repeated TLS/connection setup to Bedrock. Temperature affects output randomness, not latency; guardrail denied topics are a safety control.
